engine_loading.subtitle.focus: Bolding word anchors and laying out pages…
engine_loading.subtitle.scroll: Preparing a continuous text flow for you to glide through…
loading_fact.0: The average adult reads at 200–250 WPM. With training, 400–600 WPM is comfortable.
loading_fact.1: Speed reading reduces “saccades” — the rapid eye jumps between words that slow you down.
loading_fact.2: Sub-vocalization (silently saying words in your head) caps you around 300 WPM. Beating it is the next jump.
loading_fact.3: Comprehension typically drops above 600 WPM. Find your sweet spot.
loading_fact.4: The Guinness record for reading is over 1,000 WPM with full comprehension.
loading_fact.5: Only about 4% of your reading time is spent absorbing meaning — the rest is eye movement.
loading_fact.6: Your eye fixates on a word for ~250ms. Speed reading shortens this window.
loading_fact.7: Reading in larger chunks (4–7 words at once) can double your speed without losing meaning.
loading_fact.8: A page of dense prose averages ~250 words. Knowing this helps you pace yourself.
loading_fact.9: Skimming and speed reading are different — speed reading aims for full comprehension.
loading_fact.10: The Optimal Recognition Point (ORP) sits at ~33% of each word, where your eye naturally rests.
loading_fact.11: Most people regress 5–15% of the time, re-reading what they already read. Speed modes prevent this.
loading_fact.12: Reading on screen is ~25% slower than reading on paper, on average — focus modes close the gap.
loading_fact.13: Focus highlights the first 40% of each word — your brain fills in the rest from context.
loading_fact.14: Bolded prefixes act as visual anchors, helping your eye land precisely on each word.
loading_fact.15: The first letters of a word carry more information than the last. Focus mode leans into this.
loading_fact.16: Tap a [Tap to view…] placeholder in Focus to see the original image, table, or equation.
loading_fact.17: Scroll mode is a teleprompter — text flows past while your eyes stay still.
loading_fact.18: The yellow centre line is your fixation point. Let words come to you.
loading_fact.19: Adjust speed independently of WPM in Scroll mode — handy for skimming.
loading_fact.20: Scroll uses GPU-accelerated transforms, so it stays smooth even on long documents.

limitations.1.title: Scanned PDFs
limitations.1.body: Free version reads only digital text. Scanned or image-only PDFs require the OCR Vision add-on.
limitations.2.title: DRM-protected files
limitations.2.body: Kindle (.azw), Adobe Digital Editions (.acsm), and other DRM-locked files cannot be read.
limitations.3.title: Multi-column documents
limitations.3.body: Two-column academic papers (IEEE, ACM) may have reading-order issues in speed modes.
limitations.4.title: Tables and images
limitations.4.body: Not read word-by-word. Shown as [Object — Tap to View] placeholders. Switch to Normal View to see them.
limitations.5.title: Math equations
limitations.5.body: Skipped or shown as [Equation — Tap to View] placeholders.
limitations.6.title: Handwriting
limitations.6.body: This app is designed for printed text. Cursive or handwritten notes may not be accurately recognised even with OCR.
limitations.7.title: OCR accuracy (Image / Scan)
limitations.7.body: On-device OCR works best on flat, well-lit printed text photographed straight-on. Accuracy drops with poor lighting, angle, or low resolution.
limitations.8.title: Password-protected PDFs
limitations.8.body: Detected at import. A clear error message is shown.
limitations.9.title: RTL languages
limitations.9.body: Currently optimised for left-to-right languages only. Arabic, Hebrew, and Urdu are not supported in v1.
limitations.10.title: Offline dictionary coverage
limitations.10.body: Pro tier dictionary contains ~150k common words. Specialist terms may not be found.
limitations.11.title: URL reader (Pro)
limitations.11.body: Requires internet for the initial article fetch. The text is then saved offline.

calibration.sample: FlowRead is built for readers who want less friction and more momentum. The goal of this calibration is not to impress you with a big number — it’s to find the pace where reading feels effortless. Start slow, watch the words land, and nudge the speed up until it feels natural.
